messages:
Amelia Chen: Heads-up: follow-up from yesterday's RFC — we need a short working session to decide the canonical labels for inference metrics across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. current ad-hoc tags are making cross-team cost queries horrible.
Vikram Patel: +1. Are we narrowing to a single canonical key or a layered scheme? e.g. `service.inference.model`, `inference.variant`, `inference.hardware`?
Sophia Ruiz: I prefer layered. single key loses semantics (model vs runtime variant). layering lets us do rollups: by model, by hardware class, by customer.
Amelia Chen: Agreed on layered. main requirements: 1) cheap to emit on hot path 2) stable for long-term rollups 3) compact for storage (we're sending these on every token event).
Darren Lee: Important: Dedicated customers want to attribute cost to contract id/reservation. We need a `tenant.contract_id` or similar that doesn't change during the job.
Vikram Patel: Pushing heavy strings per token is bad. Proposal: emit short numeric ids for hot path (`m_id`, `v_id`, `h_id`) and resolve to labels at ingest/enrichment. lightweight on the wire, full labels in analytics.
Sophia Ruiz: That matches previous telemetry patterns. But we must guarantee a stable ID namespace (per-deployment and per-model registry). otherwise resolution will be wrong.
Amelia Chen: Actionable proposal: canonical label set = ["m_id","v_id","h_id","runtime_tier","tenant.contract_id","route"]. m_id/v_id/h_id are integers. runtime_tier = one of [hosted,dedicated,private]. route = API route name (for token breakdown).
Vikram Patel: For cost attribution, we also want `batch_size_hint` and `quantization_profile` but those can be optional metadata emitted at session start, not per-token.
Sophia Ruiz: Agree. We'll emit session-level attributes to avoid repeated churn. Schema example (session start payload):
```json
{"session_id":"s_123","m_id":102,"v_id":5,"h_id":2,"runtime_tier":"dedicated","tenant.contract_id":"c_202","batch_size_hint":8,"quantization_profile":"q4_0"}
```
Amelia Chen: Nice. Ingest side: enrichment service will map m_id/v_id/h_id -> canonical labels and attach them to metric/doc streams. Need TTL for registry entries and versioning.
Darren Lee: How do we handle fallback when registry misses id? (deploy races/crash)
Vikram Patel: Fallback plan: if missing, tag `_unresolved:true` and include raw textual hints (model name) once, but drop for per-token emit. That will let the enrich job backfill when registry becomes available.
Sophia Ruiz: On retention/cost, mapping table should be stored in a small key-value store replicated in the ingest path for quick resolution; if not available, fall back to async enrichment with `_unresolved` markers.
Amelia Chen: Can we standardize the integer ranges? e.g., m_id = 1..1e9, v_id appended as higher bits? Or keep simple separate ints to avoid bit logic.
Vikram Patel: Keep separate ints. Simpler and avoids bit ops in C++ runtime. Storage overhead negligible.
Amelia Chen: OK. Final open items: 1) exact attribute names (we agreed) 2) registry API contract + versioning 3) ingest enrichment SLA and retry semantics 4) doc for SDK emitters (how to emit session payload + per-token ids).
Sophia Ruiz: I'll draft the registry API sketch and add a compatibility header `x-registry-version` for forward compatibility.
Darren Lee: I'll write the ingest enrichment SLA draft (max 5min backfill window, mark unresolved until enriched).
Vikram Patel: I'll update runtime SDK to emit session start payload and per-token `m_id/v_id/h_id` as ints (small PR).
Amelia Chen: Thanks — can we have PRs/mini RFCs by EOD Friday? I'll schedule a 30m sync next Tue to lock naming and rollout plan. :thumbsup:
